turns.prompt: how do the ghost sprites work? looks like its a single whitetile for them all
turns.reply:
Yes. All four ghosts share one white body texture, and the game colours each one when it draws it.

**How it's built**
- **Drawing** (`src/scenes/BootScene.js:283`): `makeGhosts()` draws the body from the `GHOST_TOP` and `GHOST_SKIRT` pixel masks into a 16x16 texture, in pure white (`0xffffff`). It makes two skirt frames, `ghost-0` and `ghost-1`, for the wiggle animation.
- **Colouring** (`src/scenes/GameScene.js:215`): each ghost gets `body.setTexture(\`ghost-${skirt}\`).setTint(COLORS.ghosts[gh.name])`. Tinting multiplies the texture's colour, so white comes out exactly as the tint colour. The colours are in `src/config.js:17`: blinky red, pinky pink, inky cyan, clyde orange. The menu (`MenuScene.js:23`) and the hall (`HallScene.js:51`) do the same, and so does the canvas renderer in `src/systems/screenImage.js:86`.
- **Eyes** (`eyes-up`, `eyes-down`, `eyes-left`, `eyes-right`): a separate sprite drawn on top of the body, never tinted. That's why they stay white and blue on every ghost, and why a ghost that has been eaten shows only its eyes.
- **Frightened ghosts** (`ghost-fright-0/1`, `ghost-flash-0/1`): these already have their colours drawn in (blue, or white while flashing, plus the face). The tint is cleared for them (`clearTint()`).

**What this means for Max**
- **Shading still works.** He can shade `assets/ghost-0.png` and `ghost-1.png` in greys. Pure white becomes the full ghost colour and darker greys become darker shades of it, so one sheet still covers all four ghosts.
- **Fixed colours don't survive.** Any colour he paints into those two files gets multiplied by the tint.
- **Per-ghost art needs a code change.** If he wants a different sprite for each ghost, the code would need to load per-ghost textures (e.g. `ghost-blinky-0`) and drop the tint. That's a small change if you want it.

No code changed this turn. The required making-of log update is in [fischerq/ludumdare60#22](https://github.com/fischerq/ludumdare60/pull/22), so there's nothing to playtest. Plan usage is at 4% of the 5-hour limit and 18% of the weekly one.

I haven't changed any code yet. This reworks the art system, so the repo rules say to ask first. Here's what I found and what I need to know.

**Pac-Man moving left:** yes, the sprite is rotated, not flipped. Moving left turns it 180°, so it's upside down. You can't see that on today's plain yellow circle, but it will show on any art with an eye or shading. The same happens in all three places that draw Pac-Man: the maze, the hall and the game picture on the cabinet screen. The spare-life icons are also drawn turned 180°.

**Where characters appear now:** the maze, the menu and the cabinet screen all draw the same sprites. The hall reuses them too: the ghost visitors are the white tinted body plus an eyes overlay and a cap overlay. Max hasn't edited any character files yet, so changing them won't overwrite his work.

**Questions** (the default I'd use is in brackets):

1. **What "layers" get their own sprites?** [Two sets now. The maze set is also used by the menu and the cabinet screen. The hall gets its own set. They live in per-layer folders like the tilesets: `assets/maze/pac-0.png`, `assets/arcade/pac-0.png`. The CRT layer gets a set once it's designed.]
2. **Ghost files:** one file per frame, like everything else now, or one strip image per character with frames side by side? [One file per frame: `maze/ghost-blinky-0`, `maze/ghost-blinky-1`, and so on, with the colours drawn into the file and no tinting.]
3. **Ghost eyes in the maze:** keep the separate eyes overlay, or draw the eyes into each ghost's own frames? [Keep the overlay, shared by all ghosts, because it's also shown on its own after a ghost is eaten. Frightened and flashing ghosts stay one shared set too.]
4. **32x32 placeholders:** the rules forbid upscaling, so I'd redraw all the code-drawn character art natively at 32x32. That covers Pac-Man, the 10 death frames, ghosts, eyes and frightened ghosts. [Yes. Pellets, the coin and the joystick stay as they are.]
5. **Pac-Man up and down in the maze:** [moving left is a flip of the right-facing frames. Up and down keep rotating the right-facing frames by 90°, with no separate up/down art.]
6. **Hall character size:** the hall is zoomed 4x and shows characters one tile big. At that size, 32x32 art would be shrunk to half its resolution and look finer-grained than the room. [Show hall characters two tiles big (2x2), so a 32x32 sprite is shown at full resolution. The alternative is 16x16 art just for the hall.]
7. **Hall frames:** the hall is top-down, like a Pokémon game. [Pac-Man and each ghost visitor get frames per direction: right and left by flipping, separate up and down drawings, 2 walk frames each. The cap is drawn into the visitor sprites, and the `visitor-cap` overlay goes.]
8. **Spare-life icons and menu:** [Use `maze/pac-2` facing left by flipping, as above.]

If the defaults are fine, just say "defaults". I'll write the scope into `design/systems/art.md` and build it as a few small commits: flip fix first, then the per-ghost files, then the 32x32 redraw, then the hall set.

The making-of log is pushed, and I merged the latest `main` into the branch. It's all in [fischerq/ludumdare60#22](https://github.com/fischerq/ludumdare60/pull/22). Plan usage is at 4% of the 5-hour limit and 18% of the weekly one.
